Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 62, verse 1:

Page 3
(Surat al-Jumu'ah)
It has eleven verses and is Madani.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah, the Sovereign, the Holy, the Mighty, the Wise.﴾

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah, the Sovereign, the Holy, the Mighty, the Wise.﴾

The connection of this surah with what precedes it is that He, exalted is He, said at the beginning of that surah: "Glorified Allah" (sabbaha lillah) in the past tense, and that does not indicate glorification in the future. So He said at the beginning of this surah in the present/future form (yusabbihu) to indicate glorification in the present and the future. As for the connection of the first to the last, it is that He, exalted is He, mentioned at the end of that surah that He would support the people of faith until they became dominant over the disbelievers, and this is in accordance with wisdom, not out of need for it, since He is absolutely self-sufficient and exalted above what the ignorant imagine in the horizons. At the beginning of this surah there is an indication, by consensus, that He is sanctified and exalted above what does not befit His lofty presence. Then, if the creation of the heavens and the earth in their entirety is in glorification of the presence of Allah, exalted is He, then to Him belongs the dominion, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah; to Him belongs the dominion﴾, and there is no dominion greater than this, which is that He is their Creator and Owner, and all of them are in the grip of His power and under His disposal, glorifying Him in the hours of the night and the ends of the day, and indeed in all times, as passed at the beginning of that surah. And since the entire dominion belongs to Him, He is the King (al-Malik) in the absolute sense; and since everything is by His creation, He is the Owner (al-Malik/al-Malik's owner), and the owner and the king are more noble than the owned, so He is characterized by attributes from which nobility arises, and there is no room for what contradicts them among the attributes, so He is Holy (al-Quddus). Thus the word "al-Malik" is an indication of affirming what is among the lofty attributes, and the word ﴿al-Quddus﴾ is an indication of negating what is not among them. And it is reported from al-Ghazali that "al-Quddus" is the One exalted above what occurs to the minds of His friends, and its explanation has already passed. Likewise ﴿al-Aziz al-Hakim﴾. Then the attributes mentioned have been read in the nominative as praise, meaning: He is the King, the Holy, the Mighty, the Wise. Had they been read in the accusative it would also be valid, like the saying of the Arabs: "Praise belongs to Allah, the People of Praise." Thus al-Zamakhshari mentioned it in al-Kashshaf. Then there are several discussions concerning the verse:

The first: He, exalted is He, said ﴿yusabbihu lillah﴾ and did not say yusabbihu Allah. What is the benefit? We say: this is among what occurs with two wordings, like shakarahu and shakara lahu, and nasahahu and nasaha lahu.

The second: ﴿al-Quddus﴾ is among the negative attributes, and it has been said that its meaning is "the Blessed."

The third: the word "al-Hakim" is also applied to others, as it was said of Luqman that he was wise. We say: al-Hakim, according to the people of verification, is the One who places things in their proper places, and Allah, exalted is He, is Wise in this sense.

Then, after He, exalted is He, finished with tawhid and tanzih, He began on prophethood, saying:

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 62, verse 2:**

﴿It is He who sent among the unlettered (al-ummiyyin, those without scripture) a messenger from among themselves, who recites to them His verses, purifies them, and teaches them the Book and wisdom, though before that they were surely in clear error.﴾

Al-ummi (unlettered) is ascribed to the nation of the Arabs, because they are an unlettered nation, having no scripture, and they neither read a book nor write. Ibn 'Abbas said: "He means those who have neither a scripture nor a prophet sent among them." It was also said: "The unlettered are those who remain upon what they were created upon," and its explanation has already passed. It is also read al-ummin (without the ya' of nisba, the relative suffix). As He, exalted is He, said: ﴿a messenger from among themselves﴾, meaning Muhammad (ﷺ). His lineage is from their lineage, and he is of their kind, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿There has certainly come to you a messenger from among yourselves﴾ [al-Tawba: 128]. The people of the meanings (ahl al-ma'ani, the scholars who explain the sense of words and structures) said: He (ﷺ) was also unlettered, like the nation among whom he was sent. The good news of him had preceded in the scriptures that he would be the unlettered Prophet. His being of this description is further removed from the suspicion that he gained the wisdom he brought by means of writing. Thus his condition was in keeping with the condition of the nation among whom he was sent, and that is closer to the truth of him.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿who recites to them His verses﴾, that is, His clear signs which make clear his message and manifest his prophethood. It is not far-fetched that the verses are those verses from which the legal rulings appear, and by which truth is distinguished from falsehood. ﴿And purifies them﴾, that is, cleanses them from the filth of polytheism and the filth of whatever else there is of sayings and deeds. According to some, (yuzakkihim) means: he reforms them, meaning he calls them to follow that by which they become pure and God-fearing. ﴿And teaches them the Book and wisdom﴾. The Book is what is recited of the verses, and wisdom is the obligatory duties. It was said: wisdom is the Sunnah, because he used to recite to them His verses and teach them His ways. It was said: the Book is the verses in their literal wording, and wisdom is the meanings deposited within them. It is not far-fetched to say: the Book is the verses of the Qur'an, and wisdom is the way of holding fast to them. As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿though before that they were surely in clear error﴾, it is evident, because they were worshippers of idols, and they were in clear error, which is polytheism. So the Messenger (ﷺ) called them to monotheism and to turning away from what they were in.

In this verse there are discussions:

The first: the People of the Book (ahl al-kitab, Jews and Christians) argued with it. They said: His saying: ﴿He sent among the unlettered a messenger from among them﴾ indicates that he, peace be upon him, was a messenger only to the unlettered, namely the Arabs specifically. However, this is weak, for it does not follow from singling out a thing for mention that what is other than it is negated. Do you not see His saying, exalted is He: ﴿nor did you write it with your right hand﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 48]? It is not understood from it that he wrote it with his left hand. And because, if he were a messenger only to the Arabs, His saying, exalted is He: ﴿as a messenger to all mankind, bearing good news and warning﴾ [Saba': 28] would not fit that. There is no room for this, since they agreed on that, and it is the truth of a restricted message. So His saying, exalted is He: ﴿to all mankind﴾ is evidence that he, peace be upon him, was a messenger to everyone.

[Page 5]

Then God, exalted is He, said: "And others among them who have not yet joined them. He is the Almighty, the Wise" (62:3). "That is the bounty of God, which He gives to whom He wills, and God is the Possessor of great bounty" (62:4).

"And others" is a conjunction with "the unlettered ones" (al-ummiyyin). The meaning is that He sent (the Messenger) to others among them. The exegetes said: they are the non-Arabs (al-a'ajim), meaning anyone other than Arabs, whatever group they may be. This is said by Ibn 'Abbas and a group. Muqatil said: it means the Successors (al-tabi'un) from this community who did not join their earlier generation. In sum, the meaning of all these statements is included in it: everyone who entered Islam after the Prophet (ﷺ) until the Day of Resurrection. Thus the unlettered ones (al-ummiyyin) refers to the Arabs, and "others" refers to those other than them from among the nations.

His words "and others" are in the genitive case because they are conjoined to the genitive noun "the unlettered ones." It is also permissible for it to be in the accusative, as a conjunction with the accusative object in "and teaches them" (yu'allimuhum), meaning: and He teaches them and teaches others from among them, i.e., from among the unlettered ones. He made them (the others) "from among them" because when they embrace Islam they become of them. All Muslims are one community even if their races differ. God, exalted is He, said: "The believing men and the believing women are allies of one another" (9:71). As for one who did not believe in the Prophet (ﷺ) and did not enter his religion, such people are outside the scope of His words "and others from among them," even though the Prophet was sent to them with the call. Indeed, He, exalted is He, said in the first verse: "and purifies them and teaches them the Book and the Wisdom," and non-believers are not among those whom He teaches the Book and the Wisdom. "(He is the Almighty)" in that He placed in every human being the trace of humility before Him and need for Him; "the Wise" in that He placed in every creature that which testifies to His oneness.

As for His words, exalted is He: "That is the bounty of God, which He gives to whom He wills, and God is the Possessor of great bounty." Ibn 'Abbas said: He means that He joined the non-Arabs and their sons to the Quraysh, i.e., when they believe they are joined in the rank of virtue to those who witnessed the Messenger, peace be upon him, and they share with them in that. Muqatil said: "That is the bounty of God" means Islam, "which He gives to whom He wills." Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: it means prophethood; the bounty of God, which He gives to whom He wills, and so He singled out Muhammad (ﷺ) with it. And God is the Possessor of great favor over all His creation in this world through teaching the Book and the Wisdom, as has passed, and in the Hereafter through magnifying the reward for deeds.

Then, exalted is He, He set forth a parable for the Jews who turned away from acting upon the Torah and from believing in the Prophet (ﷺ), saying:

"The likeness of those who were charged with the Torah, then did not bear it, is as the likeness of a donkey carrying books. Evil is the likeness of the people who denied the signs of God. And God does not guide the wrongdoing people" (62:5).

Know that when He, exalted is He, established monotheism and prophethood, and explained concerning prophethood that he, peace be upon him, was sent to the unlettered ones and to the Jews, when they raised that doubt—namely, that he, peace be upon him, was sent only to the Arabs and was not sent to them, according to the implication of the verse—God, exalted is He, followed it with the setting forth of a parable for those who turned away from acting upon the Torah and from believing in the Prophet, peace be upon him. The purpose of it is that since they did not act upon what is in the Torah, they were likened to a donkey, because had they acted upon its requirements they would have benefited from it and would not have raised that doubt. This is because in it is the description of the Messenger, peace be upon him, the good tidings of his coming, and entering his religion. His words "were charged with the Torah" mean they were charged with acting upon what is in it and were obliged to uphold it. "Were charged" (hummilu) is read with light and heavy pronunciation. The author of al-Nazm said: it is not from carrying on the back, but from hamalah, meaning surety and guarantee; from it the guarantor is called hamil. The meaning: they were made responsible for the rulings of the Torah, then did not take responsibility for them and did not act upon what is in them. Al-Asma'i said: "al-hamil" is the guarantor. Al-Kisa'i said: "I took on for him a hamalah," i.e., I stood surety for him. "Asfar" is the plural of "sifr," which is a large book, because it reveals meaning when read; its parallel is "shibr" and "ashbar." He likened the Jews, since they did not benefit from what is in the Torah—which points to belief in Muhammad (ﷺ)—to the donkey that carries scholarly books and does not know what is in them.

The people of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: this parable is that of one who understands the meanings of the Qur'an but does not act upon it and turns away from it as one who has no need for it. For this reason Maymun ibn Mihran said: "O people of the Qur'an, follow the Qur'an before it follows you," and then recited this verse. His words "they did not bear it" mean they did not discharge its right and did not bear it the right bearing, in the manner we have explained. So He likened them, while the Torah was in their hands and they were not acting by it, to a donkey carrying books; it has nothing from that except the weight of the load without benefit from what it carries. Likewise the Jews have from their Book nothing but the burden of proof against them. Then He censured the parable, and the purpose of it is their censure, saying: "Evil is the likeness of the people who denied the signs of God," i.e., evil is the people as a likeness, those who denied, as He said: "Evil as a likeness is the people" (7:177). The position of "alladhina" is nominative, and it may be genitive. In sum, when their lying reached such a degree—that they lied against God, exalted is He—they were at the extreme of evil and corruption, and for this reason He said: "Evil is the likeness of the people." The "signs" here are the signs indicating the validity of the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), as said by Ibn 'Abbas and Muqatil. It was also said: the signs are the Torah, because they denied it when they abandoned belief in Muhammad (ﷺ), and this is closer here. "And God does not guide the wrongdoing people": 'Ata' said: He means those who wronged themselves by denying the prophets. Here there are discussions:

The first discussion: What is the wisdom in specifying the donkey from among all other animals?

We say: for several reasons:

Among them, that He created "horses and mules and donkeys for you to ride and as adornment" (16:8). Adornment is greater and more evident in horses, in relation to riding and carrying loads upon them; in mules it is less than in horses, and in donkeys less than in mules. So mules are intermediate in the three meanings, and then it follows that the donkey is more evident and more prevalent in the meaning of carrying, in comparison with horses, mules, and other animals.

Among them: this illustration serves to show ignorance and dullness, and this is most evident in the donkey.

Among them: in the donkey there is a degree of abasement and lowliness not found in others, and the purpose of the speech in this context is to shame the people with that and belittle them; so specifying the donkey is more fitting and more appropriate.

Among them: carrying books upon the donkey is more complete, more general, easier, and safer, because it is tractable, of smooth guidance, easily led, and a foolish child can manage it without difficulty or hardship; this is among what makes its mention good in comparison with others.

Among them: observing the wording and the correspondence between words is necessary in speech, and between the two words "asfar" (books) and "himar" (donkey) there is a verbal correspondence not found with other animals, so mentioning it is preferable.

Second: What is the position of "yahmilu" (carries)? We say: it is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (hal), or in the genitive as a descriptive qualifier, as said in the Kashshaf, since the donkey is like the base person in the verse:

"I pass by the base one who reviles me, so I pass on there and say, 'He does not concern me.'"

Third: God said: "Evil is the likeness of the people." How was the parable described with this description? We say: the description, although apparently applied to the parable, actually refers to the people; it is as though He said: "Evil are the people as a people whose likeness is thus."

The people of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: this parable is that of one who understands the meanings of the Qur'an but does not act upon it and turns away from it as one who has no need for it. For this reason Maymun ibn Mihran said: "O people of the Qur'an, follow the Qur'an before it follows you," and then recited this verse. His words "they did not bear it" mean they did not discharge its right and did not bear it the right bearing, in the manner we have explained. So He likened them, while the Torah was in their hands and they were not acting by it, to a donkey carrying books; it has nothing from that except the weight of the load without benefit from what it carries. Likewise the Jews have from their Book nothing but the burden of proof against them. Then He censured the parable, and the purpose of it is their censure, saying: "Evil is the likeness of the people who denied the signs of God," i.e., evil is the people as a likeness, those who denied, as He said: "Evil as a likeness is the people" (7:177). The position of "alladhina" is nominative, and it may be genitive. In sum, when their lying reached such a degree—that they lied against God, exalted is He—they were at the extreme of evil and corruption, and for this reason He said: "Evil is the likeness of the people." The "signs" here are the signs indicating the validity of the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), as said by Ibn 'Abbas and Muqatil. It was also said: the signs are the Torah, because they denied it when they abandoned belief in Muhammad (ﷺ), and this is closer here. "And God does not guide the wrongdoing people": 'Ata' said: He means those who wronged themselves by denying the prophets. Here there are discussions:

The first discussion: What is the wisdom in specifying the donkey from among all other animals?

We say: for several reasons:

Among them, that He created "horses and mules and donkeys for you to ride and as adornment" (16:8). Adornment is greater and more evident in horses, in relation to riding and carrying loads upon them; in mules it is less than in horses, and in donkeys less than in mules. So mules are intermediate in the three meanings, and then it follows that the donkey is more evident and more prevalent in the meaning of carrying, in comparison with horses, mules, and other animals.

Among them: this illustration serves to show ignorance and dullness, and this is most evident in the donkey.

Among them: in the donkey there is a degree of abasement and lowliness not found in others, and the purpose of the speech in this context is to shame the people with that and belittle them; so specifying the donkey is more fitting and more appropriate.

Among them: carrying books upon the donkey is more complete, more general, easier, and safer, because it is tractable, of smooth guidance, easily led, and a foolish child can manage it without difficulty or hardship; this is among what makes its mention good in comparison with others.

Among them: observing the wording and the correspondence between words is necessary in speech, and between the two words "asfar" (books) and "himar" (donkey) there is a verbal correspondence not found with other animals, so mentioning it is preferable.

Second: What is the position of "yahmilu" (carries)? We say: it is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (hal), or in the genitive as a descriptive qualifier, as said in the Kashshaf, since the donkey is like the base person in the verse:

"I pass by the base one who reviles me, so I pass on there and say, 'He does not concern me.'"

Third: God said: "Evil is the likeness of the people." How was the parable described with this description? We say: the description, although apparently applied to the parable, actually refers to the people; it is as though He said: "Evil are the people as a people whose likeness is thus."

Then God, exalted is He, commanded the Prophet (ﷺ) with this address to them, which is:

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 62, verses 6–7:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: O you who have become Jews (hada), if you claim that you are the allies of Allah to the exclusion of other people, then wish for death, if you are truthful.﴾ ﴿But they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have sent forward. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.﴾

This verse is among what has already been explained. It has been recited as "fa-tamannawu al-mawti" (with the waw of the verb written with a kasra, reading al-mawti), and "hadu" means "tahawwadu" (they became Jews, adopted Judaism). They used to say: "We are the sons of Allah and His beloved." So if their claim were true and they were certain of it, they would wish of Allah that He cause them to die and quickly transfer them to the abode of His honor, which He prepared for His allies. The poet said:

He who has died and found rest is not a dead man; the dead man is the dead among the living.

So they would necessarily seek death if the situation were as they claimed. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have sent forward﴾ means: because of what they had sent forward of disbelief and distortion of the verses. His saying, ﴿And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers﴾ means: of their wrongdoing, through their distortion of the verses, their obstinacy toward them, and their arrogant rejection of them.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 62, verse 8:

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: Indeed, the death from which you flee will surely meet you. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do.﴾

This means: the death from which you flee, because of what your hands have put forward, such as distorting the verses and other things, will surely meet you without doubt, and fleeing will not benefit you. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed. This means: He knows what He made the creation witness of the Torah and the Gospel, and He knows what you hid from the creation of the description of Muhammad (ﷺ), and what you concealed within yourselves of your denial of his message. As for His saying, ﴿then He will inform you of what you used to do﴾, it is either directly, in a manner connected with your meeting on the Day of Resurrection, or through the recompense: if it is good, then it is good, and if it is evil, then it is evil. So His saying, ﴿Indeed, the death from which you flee﴾, is an alert to striving for what benefits you in the Hereafter, and His saying, ﴿then He will inform you of what you used to do﴾, is an eloquent warning and a severe threat. Then, in the verse there are discussions:

The first discussion: He introduced the fa' (then/so) because it carries the meaning of a condition and a consequence. In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud, it is ﴿mulaqikum﴾ without ﴿fa-innahu﴾ (so indeed it).

Page 8

The second: it may be said: death will meet them in every state, whether they flee or do not flee, so what is the meaning of the condition and the consequence? It is said: this is by way of refuting them, since they thought that fleeing would save them. He stated this meaning explicitly and made it clear with the real condition in His saying:

Whoever dreads the causes of death, death will reach him, even if he climbs the causes of the sky by a ladder.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 62, verses 9–10:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, when the call is made for the prayer on the day of Friday, then hasten to the remembrance of Allah and leave off trade. That is better for you, if you only knew.﴾ ﴿And when the prayer has been concluded, disperse within the land and seek of the bounty of Allah, and remember Allah often that you may be successful.﴾

The connection with what came before is that the Jews flee from death for the enjoyment of this world and its pleasures, and those who believe likewise sell and buy for the enjoyment of this world and its pleasures. So Allah, may He be exalted, alerted them with His saying, ﴿then hasten to the remembrance of Allah﴾, meaning: towards that which benefits you in the Hereafter, which is attending the Friday prayer, because this world and its enjoyments are perishing, while the Hereafter and what is in it are everlasting. Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿But the Hereafter is better and more enduring﴾ [Al-A'la: 17].

Another connection: some of them said: Allah has refuted the claims of the Jews in three respects. They boasted that they are the friends and beloved of Allah, so He refuted them with His saying: ﴿So wish for death, if you are truthful﴾. And [they boasted] that they are the People of the Book, while the Arabs have no book, so He likened them to a donkey carrying books. And [they boasted] of the Sabbath, while the Muslims had no equivalent, so Allah, may He be exalted, legislated for them the Friday.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿when it is called﴾ refers to the call (adhan) when the imam sits upon the pulpit on the day of Friday. This is the view of Muqatil. He is right in what he said, because during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) there was no call at that time; when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sat upon the pulpit, Bilal would call to prayer at the door of the mosque. The same was the case during the time of Abu Bakr and 'Umar.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿for the prayer﴾ means: for the time of the prayer. This is indicated by His saying: ﴿from the day of Friday﴾, and the prayer is not from the day, rather its time is from the day.

Al-Layth said: Friday (al-Jumu'ah) is a day specified for the gathering of people on it. It is pluralized as al-Juma'at and al-Juma'. On the authority of Salman, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Friday was named Friday because Adam was gathered in it, his creation (was completed)." It is also said: because Allah finished in it the creation of things, so the creatures gathered in it.

Al-Farra' said: There are three dialectal forms of it: the lightened form (al-Jumu'ah), which is the reading of al-A'mash, and the heavy form (al-Jummu'ah), which is the reading of the majority, and a dialect of Bani 'Uqayl.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿then hasten to the remembrance of Allah﴾ means: then proceed. It is also said: then walk. On this view, the meaning of sa'y (hastening) is walking, not running. Al-Farra' said: proceeding, hastening and going are of one meaning.

On the authority of 'Umar, that he heard a man reciting "fas'aw" (hasten). He said: Who taught you this? He said: Ubayy. He said: He never stops reciting the abrogated (al-mansukh, that which has been abrogated). If it were "fas'aw," I would have hastened until my cloak fell off.

It is also said: the intended meaning of sa'y is intention, not running. Sa'y is the undertaking of any work. From this is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿When he reached with him the sa'y﴾ [As-Saffat: 102]. Al-Hasan said: By Allah, it is not walking on the feet; rather it is hastening with the hearts, hastening with intention, hastening with desire, and similar. Hastening here is, according to some, action; this is the position of Malik and al-Shafi'i, since sa'y in the Book of Allah means action. He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And when he turns away, he strives (sa'a) in the land﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 205], and ﴿Indeed, your efforts (sa'yakum) are diverse﴾ [Al-Layl: 4], meaning: your actions.

It is narrated from him (ﷺ): "When you come to the prayer, do not come to it hastening, but come to it with tranquility upon you." The jurists agreed that the Prophet (ﷺ), whenever he came to the Friday prayer, came at a calm pace.

His saying: ﴿to the remembrance of Allah﴾. The remembrance (dhikr) is, according to most of the exegetes (ahl al-tafsir), the sermon (khutbah). It is also said: it is the prayer. As for the rulings related to this verse, they are known from the books of jurisprudence (fiqh).

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿and leave off trade﴾. Al-Hasan said: When the caller calls on the day of Friday, buying and selling become unlawful. 'Ata' said: When the sun has passed its zenith, buying and selling become unlawful. Al-Farra' said: Buying and selling became unlawful only when the call for prayer is made, because of the place of gathering and so that they may attain all the good deeds in full.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿That is better for you﴾ means: in the Hereafter. ﴿if you only knew﴾ means: what is better for you and more beneficial.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when the prayer has been concluded﴾ means: when you have performed the obligatory prayer on the day of Friday. ﴿then disperse within the land﴾. This is an imperative form with the meaning of permission (ibahah), because the permission to disperse had ceased with the obligation of performing the prayer. When that ends, permission returns, so it is permitted for them to scatter across the land and seek of the bounty of Allah, which is provision. A parallel is His saying: ﴿There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 198].

Ibn 'Abbas said: When you have finished the prayer, if you wish, go out; if you wish, pray until 'Asr; if you wish, sit. Likewise His saying: ﴿and seek of the bounty of Allah﴾, for it is also an imperative form with the meaning of permission, for the acquisition of provision through trade after the prohibition by His saying: ﴿and leave off trade﴾.

On the authority of Muqatil: He permitted them to seek provision after the prayer; whoever wishes goes out, and whoever wishes does not go out. Mujahid said: If he wishes, he does; if he wishes, he does not. Al-Dahhak said: It is a permission from Allah, may He be exalted, when one has finished; if he wishes he goes out, and if he wishes he sits.

The best way of seeking of the bounty of Allah is to seek provision, or a righteous child, or beneficial knowledge, and other good things. The apparent meaning is the first.

On the authority of 'Irak ibn Malik: when he had prayed the Friday prayer, he would turn and stand at the door of the mosque and say: "O Allah, I have answered Your call, I have performed Your obligation, and I have dispersed as You commanded me. So provide me from Your bounty, and You are the best of providers."

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿and remember Allah often﴾. Muqatil said: with the tongue. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: with obedience. Mujahid said: one is not among those who remember Allah much until he remembers Him standing, sitting and lying on his side. The meaning is: when you return to trade and turn once again to buying and selling, then remember Allah often. He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Men whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah﴾ [An-Nur: 37].

On the authority of 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "When you come to the market, say: There is no god but Allah, alone, without partner; to Him belongs dominion and to Him belongs praise; He gives life and causes death, and He is over all things competent. Whoever says it, Allah will record for him a thousand thousand good deeds, remove from him a thousand thousand sins, and raise for him a thousand thousand degrees."

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿that you may be successful﴾ is among what has passed many times.

In the verse there are several discussions.

The first: What is the wisdom in Allah, may He be exalted, prescribing this obligation on the day of Friday? We say: Al-Qaffal said: It is that Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, created the creation and brought them from non-existence into existence, and made some of them inanimate, some growing, and some animate. Other than the inanimate are of various kinds: among them are beasts, angels, jinn and humans. Then they differ in their dwellings, from the high and the low. The most noble of the lower world are humans, because of their wondrous composition, and because of what Allah, may He be exalted, honored them with, namely speech, and He placed in them intellects and natures by which the highest form of worship through the laws is attained. He did not hide the greatness of the favor and the magnitude of the gift bestowed upon them. So they were commanded to give thanks for this honor on one of the seven days in which the creatures were produced and their existence completed, so that in their gathering on that day there would be a reminder of the greatness of what Allah, may He be exalted, has bestowed upon them. Since their state has not been free, from the time they began, of blessing that permeates them, and since Allah's favor is established upon them before they deserved it, and for every people of the known religions there is a day that is held in honor: for the Jews it is Saturday, for the Christians it is Sunday, and for the Muslims it is Friday. It is narrated from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "The day of Friday is the day about which they differed, and Allah guided us to it. So for the Jews is tomorrow (Saturday), and for the Christians is the day after tomorrow (Sunday)." Since the day of Friday was made a day of thanks, of displaying joy and magnifying the blessing, gathering was needed on it, by which its fame is spread, so congregations were formed for it, as is the sunnah for festivals. The sermon was needed on it as a reminder of the blessing and an incitement to sustain it by performing what returns the bounties of gratitude. And since the core of the magnification lies in the prayer, the prayer was set for this day in the middle of the day so that the gathering would be complete, and this prayer was not valid except in one mosque, so that it would be more conducive to gathering. And Allah knows best.

The second: How was the remembrance of Allah specified as the sermon, when the sermon includes the remembrance of Allah and other than Allah? We say: The intended meaning of the remembrance of Allah is the sermon and the prayer, because each of them includes the remembrance of Allah. As for what is beyond that, such as mention of the oppressors, praising them and invoking blessings upon them, that is the remembrance of Satan.

The third: His saying: ﴿and leave off trade﴾. Why did He specify trade above all other actions? We say: Because it is among the most important things a person occupies himself with during the day for the sake of livelihood. In it there is an indication of abandoning commerce. Also, buying and selling in markets is usual, and heedlessness is most prevalent among the people of the market. So His saying: ﴿and leave off trade﴾ is an alert to the heedless, and therefore trade is more appropriate to mention. It was not forbidden in itself, but because of the distraction it causes from the obligation, so it is like prayer in usurped land.

The fourth: What is the difference between the first remembrance of Allah and the second remembrance of Allah? We say: The first is among the things that cannot be combined with trade at all, since what is intended by it is the sermon and the prayer, as has passed. The second is among the things that can be combined with it, as in His saying: ﴿Men whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah﴾.

We say: Al-Qaffal said: It is that Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, created the creation and brought them from non-existence into existence, and made some of them inanimate, some growing, and some animate. Other than the inanimate are of various kinds: among them are beasts, angels, jinn and humans. Then they differ in their dwellings, from the high and the low. The most noble of the lower world are humans, because of their wondrous composition, and because of what Allah, may He be exalted, honored them with, namely speech, and He placed in them intellects and natures by which the highest form of worship through the laws is attained. He did not hide the greatness of the favor and the magnitude of the gift bestowed upon them. So they were commanded to give thanks for this honor on one of the seven days in which the creatures were produced and their existence completed, so that in their gathering on that day there would be a reminder of the greatness of what Allah, may He be exalted, has bestowed upon them. Since their state has not been free, from the time they began, of blessing that permeates them, and since Allah's favor is established upon them before they deserved it, and for every people of the known religions there is a day that is held in honor: for the Jews it is Saturday, for the Christians it is Sunday, and for the Muslims it is Friday. It is narrated from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "The day of Friday is the day about which they differed, and Allah guided us to it. So for the Jews is tomorrow (Saturday), and for the Christians is the day after tomorrow (Sunday)." Since the day of Friday was made a day of thanks, of displaying joy and magnifying the blessing, gathering was needed on it, by which its fame is spread, so congregations were formed for it, as is the sunnah for festivals. The sermon was needed on it as a reminder of the blessing and an incitement to sustain it by performing what returns the bounties of gratitude. And since the core of the magnification lies in the prayer, the prayer was set for this day in the middle of the day so that the gathering would be complete, and this prayer was not valid except in one mosque, so that it would be more conducive to gathering. And Allah knows best.

The second: How was the remembrance of Allah specified as the sermon, when the sermon includes the remembrance of Allah and other than Allah? We say: The intended meaning of the remembrance of Allah is the sermon and the prayer, because each of them includes the remembrance of Allah. As for what is beyond that, such as mention of the oppressors, praising them and invoking blessings upon them, that is the remembrance of Satan.

The third: His saying: ﴿and leave off trade﴾. Why did He specify trade above all other actions? We say: Because it is among the most important things a person occupies himself with during the day for the sake of livelihood. In it there is an indication of abandoning commerce. Also, buying and selling in markets is usual, and heedlessness is most prevalent among the people of the market. So His saying: ﴿and leave off trade﴾ is an alert to the heedless, and therefore trade is more appropriate to mention. It was not forbidden in itself, but because of the distraction it causes from the obligation, so it is like prayer in usurped land.

The fourth: What is the difference between the first remembrance of Allah and the second remembrance of Allah? We say: The first is among the things that cannot be combined with trade at all, since what is intended by it is the sermon and the prayer, as has passed. The second is among the things that can be combined with it, as in His saying: ﴿Men whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah﴾.

Then Almighty God said: ﴿And when they see a trade or a diversion, they break away toward it and leave you standing. Say: What is with God is better than diversion and than trade, and God is the best of providers.﴾

Muqatil said: "Dihya ibn Khalifa al-Kalbi came with a trade caravan from Syria before he had become Muslim, and it carried all kinds of merchandise. The people of Madinah went out to meet him with drums and clapping. This happened on a Friday while the Prophet (ﷺ) was standing on the pulpit delivering the khutbah. The people went out to it and left the Prophet (ﷺ); only twelve men remained, or fewer, such as eight, or more, such as forty. He (ﷺ) said: 'Had it not been for these, I would have set the stones ablaze for them.' And the verse was revealed. Among those who were with him were Abu Bakr and Umar."

Al-Hasan said: "The people of Madinah were struck by hunger and high prices, so a caravan arrived while the Prophet (ﷺ) was delivering the khutbah on Friday. They heard of it and went out to it. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'If the last of them were to follow the first of them, the valley would blaze with fire upon them.'" Qatadah said: "They did this three times."

As for His words ﴿or a diversion﴾, it refers to the drum, and they used to play the flutes when they married off their slave-girls, so they passed by playing, and they left the Prophet (ﷺ).

His words ﴿they break away toward it﴾ mean they dispersed. Al-Mubarrad said: they inclined toward it and turned in its direction. The pronoun in ﴿toward it﴾ refers to the trade. Al-Zajjaj said: "They broke away toward him and toward it, and both meanings are the same, as in His words ﴿And seek help through patience and prayer﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:45]." The return to trade is singled out here because it was more important to them.

As for His words ﴿and leave you standing﴾, they agreed that this standing was during the Friday khutbah. Jabir said: "I never saw the Messenger of God (ﷺ) during the khutbah except that he was standing." It was asked of Abdullah: "Did the Prophet deliver the khutbah standing or sitting?" So he recited: ﴿and they left you standing﴾.

His words ﴿Say: What is with God is better﴾ mean the reward of the prayer and steadfastness with the Prophet (ﷺ), ﴿is better than diversion and than trade﴾: the diversion mentioned earlier, and the trade that Dihya brought. His words ﴿and God is the best of providers﴾ belong to the same pattern as "the best of judges" and "the best of creators." The meaning is that if providers can exist, then He is the best of providers. It was also said: the word "provider" is applied to others only in a metaphorical sense, and there is no doubt that the Provider in the true sense is better than the provider in the metaphorical sense.

There are several discussions concerning the verse:

The first discussion: trade and diversion are things that are not seen at all, and if that were so, how would ﴿when they see trade or diversion﴾ be valid? We say: what is meant is only what is close to them, namely diversion and trade, and the like, until he hears the words of God, since speech is not heard; rather, what is heard is a sound that indicates it.

The second: how does He say ﴿they break away toward it﴾ when He has mentioned two things? This has already been discussed. The author of al-Kashshaf said: its implied sense is: when they see trade, they break away toward it, or [when they see] diversion, they break away toward it; one of them is omitted because the mentioned one points to it.

The third: the words ﴿and God is the best of providers﴾ are appropriate to the trade that was mentioned, not to the diversion. We say: rather, it is appropriate to the two together, since the diversion that was mentioned was like a follower of the trade, because they showed that joy at the presence of trade, as was mentioned. And God knows best what is correct. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds, and His blessings and peace be upon our master Muhammad, and upon his family and all his companions.
